en: Jose Rizal wrote the novel Noli Me Tangere to expose the social injustices of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
Mayon Volcano in Albay features a symmetrical cone shape formed by centuries of overlapping lava and ash eruptions.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and has a thick crest of brown feathers on its head.
The Senate of the Philippines is composed of 24 senators who are elected at large by qualified voters.
The Tboli people of South Cotabato are known for weaving tnalak, a traditional cloth made from abaca fibers.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-back dance.
Ramon Barba invented a flower induction technique using potassium nitrate that increases annual mango yields in the Philippines.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system that uses marks called kudlit to change the vowel sound of a consonant.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white flower with a star-like shape, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Intramuros is a walled area within modern Manila that served as the seat of the Spanish colonial government.
Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts for his painting Spoliarium.
